proposed_from.topic:
ANCHOR_PHRASE: Support-active completeness for fixed-support systematic-selection data fusion.

ACADEMIC_FIELD: Graphical causal identification under systematic selection

MODE: gap

CLUSTER: scm

AXIS: (a)/(i)

MOTIF: M19

TARGET_TIER: field

FIELD_CONTRACT: Prove an expansion-aware support normalization and an all-branch formula-or-global-twin completeness theorem. A line-9-only patch, the terminal three-observable classification alone, or generic response-function quantifier elimination is below field.

BACKGROUND: Lee-Ghassami-Shpitser 2024 Algorithms 1-2 and Theorems 4-5 give a sound systematic-selection recursion, branchwise nonidentification results, and an explicit completeness conjecture. Tabell-Tikka-Karvanen 2026 adds general data-fusion pruning and clustering but no fixed-support selector converse. Direct primary and follow-up searches found no completion.

MODEL_REGIME: Input is a finite selector-gated semi-Markovian LS-DAG expansion G+ with explicit latent roots, selector-controlled structural equations, fixed finite alphabets, observed nodes V and random selector S, and a declared fixed selector support H. Observe the complete joint law p(V,S) on H, with epsilon-positive structurally admissible cells. Target p(Y(a,S=empty)), where do(S=empty) sets every selector intervention indicator to zero. Models share G+ and H and vary over its finite canonical response-function tables and latent-root laws.

LIVE_OPPORTUNITY: Fixed selector support changes both positive identification and nonidentification witnesses. The missing result is support normalization plus a converse that never adds an unsupplied context.

GROUNDING: Published SS-ID interleaves selection correction, district factorization, and fixing. The first changed proof step is to substitute support-constant selector gates while retaining the exact parameter image, then derive a residual rational-rule-or-common-contrast alternative whose twin compiler preserves all contexts simultaneously.

KERNEL: Define N_H(G+) as the explicit normalized response-function expansion: substitute selector components constant on H and at the target, delete only unused arguments, retain every latent root/response parameter, and mark natural-mechanism holes invoked only by the target. Prove mutual inverse parameter maps between G+ and N_H(G+) and equality of their attainable observed-target relation. Construct a terminating SA-CS-ID calculus on the normalized expansion and retained image constraints that returns exactly either (I) a rational circuit in p(V,S)|H valid for every compatible model or (II) two canonical response-table models plus an open rational parameter box, with support exactly H, identical admissible observed cells, and different targets. Prove soundness, completeness over every residual branch, preservation of valid published positive derivations, and termination by a decreasing finite state measure. A marked support-hole ancestor may terminate in II but must supply the legal pair. Projection may organize elimination but may not enlarge the model class.

FOCAL_OBJECT: The normalized explicit expansion N_H(G+), its retained parameter-image constraints, and SA-CS-ID formula-or-global-twin certificate.

COMPUTATION: Substitute fixed gates in explicit response tables; use labelled projection only to organize fixing and induced-width variable elimination; carry image constraints through recursion; verify twin tables algebraically. Exhaustively compare binary expansions through four observed nodes/two selector components with exact response-function equations at fixed H.

ESTIMATION_RUNG: Evaluate returned rational circuits with empirical p(V,S)|H; on an epsilon-positive differentiable interior derive the finite-table influence function and pointwise Wald inference. Boundary-uniform inference is delegated and not the headline.

CONSUMER: The CRAN dosearch package (Tikka-Hyttinen-Karvanen, JSS 2021, current 1.0.12) identifies effects from multiple sources and supports selection bias and context-specific independence. An optional provenance-aware CS-SCM backend would return a valid formula or exact twin/missing-context certificate without silently adding contexts.

MINIMAL_INSTANCE: Two exact binary fixed-H models in the presolve draft. With S->A,S->Y,A->Y,A<->Y,S<->Y, d=(-4,-1,0,3) preserves all six observed cells (minimum 11/96) but moves the target 1/2 to 63/128. Removing A<->Y yields an adjustment-identified neighbor with value 7/12 after inactive-gate normalization. The calculus must classify them differently without changing H.

PRIOR_ART: Lee-Ghassami-Shpitser 2024 https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06602; Tabell-Tikka-Karvanen 2026 https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v27/25-1140.html; dosearch https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v099i05. The candidate adds fixed-support parameter-image normalization and global all-branch twins. Queue/claims/bank checks found no collision.

EST_ACHIEVABLE_TIER: field

CEILING_REASON: Full support-aware constructive completeness resolves a new identification regime and changes a live software workflow; finite graph-specific scope keeps it below flagship.

LIKELY_DEATH: General residuals may require nonrational semialgebraic functionals, or common contrasts may fail to lift through interacting districts while preserving H.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Retained-parameter normalization was derived, and a complete terminal three-observable classification was proved: usable-context coverage gives identification, while a tensor-product response contrast gives every negative case. Exact arithmetic verified 78 formula cases and 78 twin cases, plus the 7/12 formula and 1/2 versus 63/128 twins. Checks covered inactive gates, natural-mechanism holes, all treatment/selection-confounding patterns, positivity, rationality risks, generic-elimination collapse, and consumer fit.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that every irreducible normalized residual admits an observable rational reduction or a common response contrast that lifts through interacting districts and fixed kernels while preserving the complete observed law and exactly H.
EARLY KILL TEST: Replay the paired examples and 156 terminal configurations through the recursion, add one observed mediator at the same two contexts, and compare every certificate with exact response-table equations; any changed observed cell/H or an identified nonrational residual forces pivot.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_fixedsupport_complete_id.md.

seed_details.seed: Support-active formula-or-global-twin completeness for fixed selector support
seed_details.question: Can every finite fixed-support context-selected SCM be decided by a terminating calculus that returns either a rational functional of the supplied joint law or a pair of support-exact canonical models that agree on every supplied cell and disagree on \(p\{Y(a,S=\emptyset)\}\)?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Before the district recursion of SS-ID, substitute selector gates that are constant on the registered observational and target executions while retaining their exact response-parameter image; on failure, replace contextwise hedge pasting by one contrast that preserves all contexts in \(H\) simultaneously.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing systematic selection, fixed selector support, global twins, and completeness found the 2024 SS-ID paper and the 2026 pruning paper, but no completed converse.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser because their Theorem 5 already constructs nonidentification models for failed SS-ID branches.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their paper explicitly leaves one failure class outside Theorem 5 and conjectures completeness; moreover, its proof does not impose a declared support \(H\), preserve all supported cells with one shared mechanism, or retain the fixed-support parameter image.

seed_details.seed: Retained-image normalization for selector-gated structural equations
seed_details.question: Does substitution of every support-constant selector gate, with dormant natural response rows retained as provenance, preserve exactly the attainable observed-target relation and admit an inverse gate-reinsertion map?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace latent projection by an execution-indexed response-table substitution and prove equality pathwise in the recursive order before marginalizing latent roots.
seed_details.destination_search: Canonical-SCM and constrained-identification searches found finite response-type compilation and arithmetic-circuit invariance, but no inverse normalization preserving known selector multiplexers on a restricted support.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from canonical response-function discretization because substituting a constant argument is syntactic simplification.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary simplification discards dormant coordinates and enlarges the projected model; the inverse-map and exact observed-target image claims require preserving selector sharing, target-only natural rows, root laws, and support constraints.
seed_details.disposition: survives as a required lemma of rank 1

seed_details.seed: If-and-only-if pruning and clustering on normalized selector images
seed_details.question: Which pruning and transit-clustering operations admit inverse lifts for both identifying formulas and support-exact twin pairs in the normalized fixed-support model?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Strengthen the graph-reduction lemma from Markov-model comparison to equality of retained response-parameter images with the same selector support.
seed_details.destination_search: The 2026 data-fusion paper proves identification invariance under sufficient graphical conditions and formula transport for do-calculus outputs, but it does not treat an endogenous selector or exact parameter-image lifts.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen because identification invariance already transfers both positive and negative conclusions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their inputs are separately supplied distributions and their model lifts do not preserve a single endogenous selector law, fixed support, support-constant gate equalities, or target-only response rows.
seed_details.disposition: survives; folded into the main calculus rather than selected alone

seed_details.seed: Sharp graph-native bounds under fixed selector support
seed_details.question: What are the sharp bounds on \(p\{Y(a,S=\emptyset)\}\) after enforcing the exact selector-gate image and forbidding distributions for contexts outside \(H\)?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compile the selector-gated canonical response tables before writing the polynomial feasible set, so shared gate coordinates and exact support are constraints rather than separately indexed source laws.
seed_details.destination_search: Canonical counterfactual bounding and biased-data fusion searches found polynomial programs for arbitrary supplied laws, but not fixed-support endogenous-selector image constraints.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim by adding the observed equations to their canonical-SCM polynomial program.
seed_details.rebuttal: Treating selector contexts as separate inputs loses the cross-context image and exact-support restriction; the new feasible set must be proved equivalent to the selector-gated SCM class and its endpoints attained within that class.
seed_details.disposition: ranked out because it weakens the live point-identification completeness target

seed_details.question: Can all inclusion-minimal supersets \(H'\supset H\) that identify the target be characterized while requiring every added context to share the original selector mechanism?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Convert a support-preserving global contrast into a hitting condition on added contexts and prove that eliminating every compiled contrast is sufficient, not merely that one displayed twin is separated.
seed_details.destination_search: do-search and general-identification work discuss additional experiments as separately available inputs; no source found treats structurally legal support augmentation of an endogenous selector.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from failed do-search states or thickets by adding any experiment that breaks the returned witness.
seed_details.rebuttal: Breaking one witness is not sufficiency, and a selector context is not a free experiment because it activates shared gates and changes the joint support restriction.
seed_details.disposition: ranked out pending the rank-1 decision theorem

seed_details.seed: Automatic influence functions for support-valid rational circuits
seed_details.question: Can each differentiable rational circuit returned by a fixed-support identifier be mapped mechanically to its finite-table influence function and a pointwise valid Wald procedure?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the circuit with respect to the one joint multinomial law on \(H\), rather than treating selector contexts as independent samples, and project the gradient onto the simplex tangent space.
seed_details.destination_search: Fixing-based and general data-fusion influence-function papers cover hidden-variable functionals or source alignment, not endogenous-selector circuits with retained image equalities.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from the ordinary multivariate delta method for a finite multinomial table.
seed_details.rebuttal: The pointwise derivative is routine once a circuit exists, so this is retained only as an estimation rung and not as the proposal kernel; the nonroutine contribution is generating only support-valid circuits.
seed_details.disposition: ranked out as a standalone seed; retained as a corollary

seed_details.seed: Width-sensitive certificate complexity for support-aware identification
seed_details.question: Can labelled projection and variable elimination yield formula or twin certificates whose construction and verification costs are fixed-parameter tractable in the induced width of the normalized response expansion?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Carry the retained selector-image constraints through each elimination bucket and compile a local common contrast without invoking unrestricted quantifier elimination.
seed_details.destination_search: Arithmetic-circuit constrained identification provides compact positive computations, while SS-ID provides graphical recursion; no searched result gives width-sensitive support-exact negative certificates.
seed_details.red_team_objection: A generic semialgebraic solver already decides every finite response-function model.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic quantifier elimination neither yields the required graph-native rational-rule-or-global-twin alternative nor a support-preserving certificate with induced-width complexity.
seed_details.disposition: ranked out because complexity should follow, rather than replace, the structural completeness theorem

seed_details.seed: Exceptional-fiber identification inside a globally nonidentified selector model
seed_details.question: For a fixed normalized expansion that is globally nonidentified, can the observed-law fibers on which the target becomes point identified be characterized by an explicit discriminant or invariant-cut condition?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After normalization, study target constancy on each fiber of the polynomial observation map rather than applying a graph-level hedge criterion uniformly over all positive laws.
seed_details.destination_search: Constrained-identification examples show that a fixed observed distribution can restore identification, but no searched work characterizes the exceptional fibers created by systematic-selection gate constraints.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Immediate from arithmetic-circuit invariance testing at a fully known observational table.
seed_details.rebuttal: An instancewise test is not a symbolic characterization of the entire exceptional locus, and the selector model imposes a smaller shared-mechanism image than the unconstrained circuit model.
seed_details.disposition: ranked out because it is secondary to global model-class completeness

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel is anchored in Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024), whose Definition 1 supplies the selector multiplexer, Algorithms 1--2 interleave district factorization, fixing, and selection correction, Theorem 4 proves soundness, Theorem 5 supplies witnesses for specified failure branches, and the text immediately preceding those theorems explicitly leaves completeness as a conjecture. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022), especially Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, show how a positivity-qualified data-fusion problem can be reduced to classical ID subproblems and how positive twin models must be rebuilt when an earlier hedge construction lies on a zero-probability face; this is the closest method exemplar for support-correct negative-certificate transport. Mokhtarian, Jamshidi, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022), Theorem 1 and its necessity proof, reduce root-control CSI identification to finitely many context-specific graph problems and couple context models through an \(\epsilon\)-mixture construction; their control variables are observed roots, unlike the endogenous selector here. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022), Theorem 1 and Appendix A, provide the finite canonical response-type reduction used to make global twins algebraic, but their inputs are arbitrary supplied observational and experimental laws rather than one selector-gated joint law on fixed \(H\). Chen and Darwiche (2024), Definitions 2--3 and Sections 4--5, formalize parameter-constrained identifiability and invariant arithmetic-circuit cuts; their general constraint examples do not provide a complete negative-certificate calculus for fixed-support selectors. Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (2026), Definition 5 and Theorems 7, 18, 20, and 21, establish sufficient identification-invariant reductions and transport do-calculus formulas, but do not retain or invert an endogenous selector's fixed-support parameter image. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) supply the ordinary formula-or-hedge completeness template. Targeted searches through September 2026 for systematic selection with fixed support, selector-support completeness, and citations of the 2024 anchor found no closer theorem; the only direct follow-up located was the 2026 pruning and clustering paper. The writing arc follows Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser: systematic assignment creates one coherent likelihood, context-specific invariances improve identification, the existing recursion is sound but incomplete, and fixed support requires a support-active converse rather than an unsupplied experiment.
